spec.title: vscode PROP-006: The brand image set - the target table and the artwork families

status.comment: the type's answer to the brand-images question of PROP-016 §2 (capability `brand-images`); the anchored facts moved verbatim from modules/codkit/PROP-007 §21 in the split of 2026-09-09. The generator, the index and the verifier stay in the engine

p.IMAGESET-TARGET-DISCOVERY: The targets are discovered, not hard-coded. The set of paths is built-in knowledge of the distribution (fixed paths and globs). The application icon: `resources/win32/code.ico`, `resources/darwin/code.icns`, `resources/linux/code.png`, `resources/win32/code_*.png`, `resources/linux/rpm/*.xpm`, `resources/server/favicon.ico`, `resources/server/code-*.png`. The installer graphics: `resources/win32/inno-big-*.bmp`, `resources/win32/inno-small-*.bmp`. The file-type icons: `resources/win32/*.ico` and `resources/darwin/*.icns` - minus `code.ico` and `code.icns`, and the subtraction is declared by an explicit `exclude` list rather than by the order of the patterns: a glob that silently took someone else's target would give two map entries for one path. The empty-editor watermarks: `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/media/letterpress-*.svg` and `src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/media/letterpress-*.svg`. A missing fixed path is printed; a glob without matches yields no target; one file captured by two patterns is `CK-E-ARTIFACT-BROKEN` and not a silent duplicate (that is a defect of the pattern table, and it has to be loud). The structure of every existing file is read from its bytes: the list of ICO frames and their sizes in directory order, the types and sizes of the ICNS elements, the sizes of BMP/XPM/PNG, the nominal size of an SVG from `width`/`height` or `viewBox` - a change upstream to the set of frames, types or sizes is picked up automatically instead of being missed. **The one exception is the declaration of the product** (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#IMAGESET-DECLARED-FRAMES`): a target whose frame set the product declares is written with the declared frames, and its shipped file only tells the reports which frames the declaration replaced. ICNS: the PNG-capable elements `ic07 ic08 ic09 ic10 ic11 ic12 ic13 ic14` are regenerated; the legacy elements (the compressed miniatures `ic04`/`ic05`, the `info` chunk) carry no PNG and are not reproduced - they are listed in the report and in `data.targets[].legacyTypes`. On the 1.135.0 upstream tree this is **84 targets and 370 required sizes**, and neither number is written down in the code.

p.IMAGESET-ICO-FRAME-SET: **ICO is the one container of this family whose frame set a product may declare.** Windows draws the icon of the executable - its taskbar button, its shortcut, the shell's views of it - from the frames of `resources/win32/code.ico` at whatever size the display scale asks for, so the frames a product ships decide how sharp its mark is there, and the pin ships 16, 32, 128 and 256 px only: at a scale of 150% the taskbar asks for about 36 px and the shell for 48, and both are made from a frame of another size. A declared ICO frame set is a non-empty list of square sizes, whole numbers from 1 to 256, each listed once; any other list is refused with the reason. The file is written as every regenerated `.ico` is (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#IMAGESET-CONTAINERS`): the frames in the declared order - the writer keeps the order it is handed, as it keeps the directory order of a shipped file - and every frame, an added one exactly like a kept one, a 32-bit RGBA PNG payload, the size 256 stored as the directory byte 0. ICNS, whose elements are named types of fixed sizes, the single-frame PNG, BMP and XPM, whose one size the layout of the distribution fixes, and SVG, a vector emitted unchanged, answer no frame set, and a frame set declared for one of their targets is refused.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-ROLE-TABLE:
**Decision:** the role of every target - "where a human sees this image" - is codkit's knowledge: it lives in the path table `packages/codkit/src/lib/imagesetTargets.ts` and is worded without the name of any downstream product.
**Why:** The role is what whoever draws needs, and it is a property of the layout of the distribution rather than of a particular product: `resources/win32/code.ico` is the icon of the executable, of the taskbar button, of the shortcut and of the file associations; `resources/win32/inno-small-*.bmp` is the header of every page of the installation wizard; `resources/linux/rpm/*.xpm` is the icon of the package in the menu of RPM distributions. codkit is a universal tool, so the name of a product in its texts would be a leak; this is checked by a test that looks for the forbidden substrings in the rendered index.
**Considered and rejected:** - keeping the roles in the product repository - every product would rewrite the same knowledge about upstream; - not writing the role at all - the index stops being a document worth handing to an agent.
**When to revisit:** when upstream adds a target whose role is not derivable from its path - then the table needs a source and not a guess.

p.IMAGESET-ARTWORK: A target names two different things, and they must not be confused. The **family** is the guard group and the masters directory: one contract test covers the whole family at once. The **artwork** is which drawing inside the family the target wants. There are five families: `icon` (one drawing over nine targets - ico, icns, png, xpm, two Start tiles, a favicon and two web-manifest icons), `installer-big` and `installer-small` (one drawing over seven targets each), `filetype` (28 drawings over 55 targets: the Windows and macOS sets overlap, and one type exists on macOS only) and `letterpress` (6 drawings over 6 targets). The master key is the family for a family with one drawing and `<family>/<artwork>` for a family with several. The identifier of the guard test is derived from the FAMILY and not from the artwork (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-GUARD-PER-FAMILY`): `guard.brand.filetype` covers all 55 file-type files instead of requiring 55 suites.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-WHOLE-BRAND-SURFACE:
**Decision:** the command covers the whole brand surface of the distribution - the application icon, the installer graphics, the file-type icons, the web client's icons and the empty-editor watermarks - and not the application icon alone.
**Why:** The owner's direction of 2026-09-06. A rebranding that left 55 file-type icons as upstream's is not a rebranding but a half-finished thing: the user sees somebody else's mark in the file explorer on every file of the project. The difference in cost is small, because the whole expensive part - the discovery of the structure, the codecs, the pipeline - is written already and does not depend on the number of targets: growing from 20 targets to 84 added a pattern table and the split between family and artwork, but not one new codec.
**Considered and rejected:** - limiting it to the application icon - it leaves the most visible part of somebody else's artwork inside the product and postpones exactly the work of splitting family from artwork that will have to be done anyway; - moving the file-type icons into a separate command - the same pipeline, the same containers, the same masters; the second command would be a copy of the first with a different list of paths.
**When to revisit:** if upstream starts loading brand artwork from a format that is neither a raster container nor an SVG - observed through a target for which neither a codec nor the vector path exists.
